w: The youths, through a program of mono-acting, presented the sacrifice and service of Dubli Bhatt and Samat Patel. They also displayed the unflinching faith and morality of devotees living today. In his blessings, Swamishri appreciated the youths for their efforts and emphasized on profoundly consolidating Satsang in one’s life.
"Some have the power to rule, some have money power and some have the power of scriptural knowledge; everyone talks of their powers but above them all is God’s power!"
"...by indulging in worldly pleasures there is no reason to believe one will become satisfied. One can only become desireless through the refuge and association of the Satpurush (holy guru)."
"No one can achieve progress without following moral disciplines."
"Today, we find that wealth has increased and comforts have also increased, so the inner nobility has gone away."

w: During the evening assembly the youths performed a lively folk dance and a drama, 'Vyasani Gokaldas'. Then in his discourse, Swamishri emphasized about the fleeting nature of everything in this world. Swamishri honored and blessed Hasan Kamal - a renowned poet.

At 10.00 a.m. Swamishri attended the murti-pratishtha yagna. Amidst Vedic chantings Swamishri performed the initial yagna rituals. The yagna had 448 couples who performed the rituals around 56 yagna pits. Swamishri performed pujan of the murtis.
In the afternoon a grand procession of floats with the murtis was carried out on the main streets of Rajula.
At 6.45 p.m. A citation was read out and a 'Key to the City' was also presented.

At 10.00 a.m. Swamishri embarked upon an observation tour of the ongoing construction work at Akshardham. Swamishri also performed pujan of the dwarshakh (frame of main entrance door of monument) and said prayers for the successful completion of complex.
During the evening satsang assemblies , Pujya Viveksagar Swami delivered lectures on the Shrimad Bhagwat and thereafter Swamishri blessed the assembly.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.

1,531 devotees pilgrimaged to Dadar mandir from different suburbs of Mumbai. Eight devotees performed 1,860 prostrations while coming to the mandir.

st.t: A Spiritual Travelogue of Pramukh Swami Maharaj - Delhi Page-6, 15 April 2004
w: Swamishri performs pujan of the Barsakh pillar amidst Vedic chanting in the presences of sadhus and devotees. After the rituals Swamishri blessed the small assembly of sadhus and devotees and then observed the inner construction of the monument.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Guru Parampara and Hanumanji and Ganapatiji for the newly built BAPS Swaminarayan hari mandirs in the villages of Langala and Umrala in the Bhavnagar district.
A youth had come for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Feeling that he was being treated unjustly in the division of property with his brothers, he had twice tried to take his own life.

This dejected youth poured out the anguish of his heart before Swamishri. Swamishri listened to him calmly. After that Swamishri said to him, "You are still young. You have many years ahead. There is a lot of life. If there is trouble in the division among brothers, it can be resolved, but what need is there to die over it? You do business, you earn money, so why lose heart? Pray to Shriji Maharaj and the dispute will be settled. Keep courage, the sorrow will not remain, and do five malas every day."
Through Swamishri's inspiring words full of strength, new hope for life awoke in that dejected youth.

ds.t: "The wise are not touched by heat"
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj was coming towards the treadmill for his walk. It was extremely hot. In this context Brahmavihari Swami said, "One month here (in Gandhinagar) is settled."
Swamishri said, "Is there any document or written agreement?"
Brahmavihari Swami said, "It is very hot everywhere. In Dhrangadhra the heat has reached 47 (C), so we are saying this."
Yogicharan Swami said, "Do this, go to Abu for a month."

Swamishri immediately said, "From the point of view of spiritual knowledge, there is neither heat nor cold. Nothing touches the one who has knowledge. The one who has knowledge has no need to go for a change of air! For him everything appears the same. However much heat there is, there is coolness."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Prof. Fritsch used to say often that you should rest for at least one month a year. Not do anything at all."
The walk had already begun, yet Swamishri replied, "Think about our tradition. Has anyone done that?"

Swamishri was speaking, but since his voice breaks when he speaks while walking, the sadhus said, "Please do not speak." So the reading of 'Swaminarayan Prakash' began. In it came the blessings Swamishri had given in Sarangpur at the time of Fuldol. There too Swamishri had said, "The one who has realised the atma is not troubled by sun or shade at all." As this came at just the right moment, Swamishri said just one word: "Listen."
The sadhus said, "But in Dhrangadhra the heat has reached 47 (C)."
Swamishri said, "Do not read such things, do not even speak of them. If there is knowledge and understanding, nothing troubles one anywhere."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Right now it seems that knowledge and understanding are only for you." (They are only in you.)
Swamishri said, "Why, do you not want liberation?"
At this question of Swamishri everyone fell silent, and the reading of 'Swaminarayan Prakash' continued.

ds.t: For the wise there is neither heat nor cold
w: Swamishri was coming to the treadmill for his walk. It was extremely hot. With this in mind Brahmavihari Swami said, "It is settled: one month here (in Gandhinagar)."
Swamishri said, "Is there a deed or something in writing?"
Brahmavihari Swami said, "It is very hot everywhere. In Dhrangadhra it has reached 47 degrees, so we are saying this."
Yogicharan Swami said, "Do this: go to Abu for a month."

Swamishri said at once, "From the view of knowledge there is neither heat nor cold. Nothing touches the wise. The wise have no need to go for a change of air! To them everything looks the same. However hot it is, there is coolness."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Prof. Fritsch used to say often that you must rest at least one month a year. Do nothing at all."
The walk had already begun, yet Swamishri replied, "Think of our tradition. Has anyone done that?"

Swamishri was speaking, but because his voice breaks when he talks while walking, the sadhus said, "Please do not speak," so a reading from 'Swaminarayan Prakash' began. In it came the blessings Swamishri had given at Sarangpur during Fuldol. There too Swamishri had said, "For one who has knowledge of the soul, neither sun nor shade troubles him." As this came at exactly the right moment, Swamishri said one word: "Listen."
The sadhus said, "But in Dhrangadhra it has reached 47 degrees."
Swamishri said, "Do not read such things, and do not speak of them either. If there is knowledge and understanding, nothing troubles anywhere."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Right now it seems knowledge and understanding are only for you." (only in you)
Swamishri said, "Why, don't you want liberation?"
At Swamishri's question everyone fell silent, and the reading of 'Swaminarayan Prakash' went on.

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his evening meal, a reading began from the book "Jena Gune Rijhya Girdhari," in which the chapter on freedom from attachment to taste was read. Based on it, Swamishri was asked, "Which dish do you like?"
Swamishri said, "All of them."
Another question was asked: "Which fruit juice suits you?"
Swamishri laughed and said, "Bitter gourd..."
Everyone laughed.
Today, addressing the sadhus who had come to put him to bed, Mahant Swami Maharaj began to say, "To see everyone as faultless is our seva. If you want to reach the heights, this is it."

Speaking of something he himself had experienced at the time of the Nagpur pratishtha, Gnanchintandas Swami said, "I had asked you, 'Please give me some niyam.' At that time too you said exactly this: 'Understand everyone as faultless, understand them as divine. This seems small but it is great.'"
"This is the essence," Swamishri said now.
Then he said, "The number one spiritual practice is seeing divinity."
